section.title: Install pmMDA
section.p: The binary distribution of pmMDA is delivered as a compressed file. Unzip the file at your preferred location. ZIP files can be opened using various open source tools. All required libraries are contained in the archive file. The installation does not need any additional steps. No environment variables or registry modifications are required. Here the steps in details.

ol.li: Download the pmMDA distribution. The file has a name with the structure pmMDA-<version>.tar.gz . Follow the download link of this site to the location of the distribution pmMDA .
Extract the distribution and store the files into a directory. To extract the files you can use free tools such as 7-zip or winzip . No need to modify startup scripts or set environment variables.
In the directory where you stored the file you will find a batch file to start the application. Simply execute the pmMDA.bat batch file by double clicking it under Windows operating system.

section.p: If you want to uninstall pmMDA distribution simply delete the directory containing the files. The installation process does not insert any data in the registry or in system directories.
section.note: You must have an installed Java Runtime Environment JRE 1.5 or Java Development Environment JDK 1.5 to run the pmMDA application. The JRE can be downloaded from Java Sun home page .
section.warning: Do not copy a new version of pmMDA over an older one. Remove the old distribution or deploy the new one in another directory. Otherwise multiple versions of libraries can be mixed up.

section.title: Run pmMDA
section.p: The script file pmMDA.bat starts the application. The user interface allows the user to open an existing model and edit it.
The example part of the pmMDA distribution provides a model. Select the open menu item in the files menu and open the file work/example/model/test-model.zargo .

You can use the context menus to modify the model and set values for tagged values. Once you are satisfied with the changes generate new code artifacts using the supplied code generator cartridges. The global menu entry generate contains the entries to call the generation routines of any configured cartridge.
section.note: You must have an installed Java Runtime Environment JRE 1.5 or Java Development Environment JDK 1.5 . You can download the environment form Java Sun home page . Define the JAVA_HOME environment variable and add the location of the java executable to your path. The environment document describes how to perform these tasks for the operation system you are using.

section.title: Generate Tests Code Artifacts
section.p: Select the the menu item Generate/Generate All . The logging information shows the progress of the artifacts generation.
You must now compile the generated artifacts before being able to run them. The next section shows how to compile the generated source code files.

section.title: Compile Tests Artifacts
section.p: Ant scripts to compile the artifacts are provided with the example under work/example/build-examples.xml . To compile the examples the following targets are provided.

dl.dd: builds the 2-tiers client using the explorer framework and connecting to the database. The client connects to the database through the O/R mapping tools.
builds the 3-tiers CORBA application with a CORBA server and a CORBA client. The client uses the explorer framework. The server connects to the database through the O/R mapping tools.
builds the 3-tiers J2EE application with a J2EE JBoss server and a J2EE client. The client uses the explorer framework. The J2EE server conects to the database through the O/R mapping tools.

section.p: The ant script is called on the command line ant -f build-examples.xml <target> where the target is one of the above mentioned ones. You must have installed JDK1.5 and ant. The environment variables JAVA_HOME and ANT_HOME must be defined.
section.note: You must have an installed Java Development Environment JDK 1.5 to compile the examples.
You must install Ant 1.6 or higher to run the compilation scripts. You can download the application form Apache Ant home page .

section.title: Run Examples
section.p: Scripts are provided to run the examples. The provided scripts allow you to run the examples in the following modes.

ul.li:
Configure the database
Create the database schema
The data definition files are generated in the directory gendir/orm-server . You should use the DDL file corresponding to the database you are using. The database must have a schema called OJB .
Set the username and password
The default username is user and the password is user . These information is configured in the ORM layer. For example when using OJB you can change this configuration in the file repository_database.xml .

Rich client scripts to run the 2-tiers application.
test-rich-client
starts the 2-tiers rich client explorer application and the connection to the database.

CORBA application scripts to run the 3-tiers CORBA application. The order of the scripts is the one of the list.
orb-start starts the CORBA ORB broker. test-corba-server
starts the CORBA server which implements the business logic and the database connection.
test-corba-client
starts the CORBA client with the rich client explorer user interface.

J2EE application scripts to run the 3-tiers J2EE application.
J2EE server EJB
No script file exists. The entreprise beans are generated in the deploy directory and copied to the deployment directory of JBoss server. The beans are copied when the artifacts are generated. So you do not need to perform any additional task.
test-j2ee-client
starts the J2EE client with the rich client explorer user interface.

section.note: You must have an installed Java Runtime Environment JRE 1.5 or Java Development Environment JDK 1.5 .
To run the J2EE JBoss mode you must have an installed version of JBoss and must configure MySQL access as follow. The needed configuration file is provided with the test distribution.

section.title: MySQL Database Configuration in JBoss 4.x
section.p: MySQL is an open source database used by many open source projects and small organizations. To use JBoss 4.0 with MySQL, we first need to put the MySQL driver classes into the CLASSPATH. Copy the .jar file mysql-connector-java-3.0.9-stable-bin.jar to the /server/default/lib directory.

To use the MySQL data source, copy /docs/examples/jca/mysql-ds.xml to the /server/default/deploy directory. Modify the mysql-ds.xml configuration file by setting <driver-class/> to com.mysql.jdbc.Driver and <connection-url/> to jdbc:mysql://<mysqlhost>/<database>, where <mysqlhost> is the MySQL host server and <database> is the MySQL database.

section.title: Prerequesites
section.p: Please read the two minutes tutorial to learn how to install pmMDA and run pmMDA application. Upon completion of these steps you are able to start the MDA application and generates artifacts.

section.title: Personal Information Manager - LDIF2VCARD converter -
section.p: The provided UML model PIM stored in models/pim-model defines the business model for a contact management application. The model contains properties, indexed properties, owned relations, changeable and vetoable properties. The stereotypes businessObject amd referenceCode are used. Examples how to define reference code values are provided. These abstractions are mapped to sophisticated Java code with the help of provided code generators.
Use ArgoUML to edit the PIM model and extend the business object model. You are free to add new abstractions or extend existing classes.

Use pmMDA to edit the tagged values used on the code generator cartridges. Do not forget to validate your changes with the build-in validator. The validator is accessible through the context menu under actions . You can generate the Java representation of the business model using the global menu Generate and the submenu bo generate . The hand coded source code defined in the protected areas of the source file is preserved.
Compile the business object classes with the service classes. If you are using Eclipse the project configuration contains all the necessary information.

section.title: Use PIM LDIF2VCARD converter
section.p: Starts the application using the command line parameters to translate your address books from LDIF format to VCARD format. Copy the VCARD file on your iPod and enjoy.

section.title: Customise Generator Templates
section.p: All generator templates are written in Velocity . All features of Velocity can be used. The items available in the context are documented in the generators documentation. Each cartridge roles, supported tagged values, attributes and properties are documented. This description is also available on the project web site.
section.warning: The runtime engine only handles correctly English identifiers. The implemented rules can only infer the singular and plural form of regular English nouns.
